name: Oliveron
body: I am sorting my wardrobe before moving, and the number of almost identical tops has become a problem. The difficulty is that each piece looks reasonable alone, yet several colors seem awkward beside my usual trousers. A compact wardrobe appeals to me, provided it allows a few different combinations instead of one repeated outfit. My first step has been comparing clothes I already own, especially combinations that can work without another purchase. I found a page about [url=https://outfit-style.top]color analysis[/url] and would like to use the idea as a starting point for these comparisons. Blue pieces get regular use, while the cream, rusty orange, and muted pink items often stay in the drawer. Is choosing two dependable neutrals a sensible starting point, or would you first look for one versatile accent color? Another question is how to tell whether a disappointing outfit comes from its color or from the garment shape. For anyone who has made a smaller wardrobe work, what test helped you choose the pieces worth keeping?
